props.title: Yi Yi

sections.content: Yi Yi (2000) stands as Edward Yang's masterful examination of urban Taiwanese life, following the Jian family through joy, tragedy, and quiet revelation. Yang's patient camera captures the interconnected stories of father NJ, teenage daughter Ting-Ting, and young son Yang-Yang with remarkable depth. Like Ozu's Tokyo Story (1953), Yi Yi finds profound meaning in everyday moments, using long takes and careful framing to let complex family dynamics unfold naturally. The film's three-hour runtime allows Yang to explore multiple generations wrestling with love, death, and purpose in modern Taipei.

sections.content: Yang's influence resonates through contemporary Asian cinema, particularly in films that examine family life with patient observation. Shoplifters (2018) by Hirokazu Kore-eda shares Yi Yi's attention to subtle family dynamics, while In the Mood for Love (2000) echoes its portrayal of urban loneliness and missed connections. The film's exploration of childhood through Yang-Yang's photography anticipates similar themes in Nobody Knows (2004) and Our Little Sister (2015).

Yi Yi's technical mastery lies in Yang's use of reflections, windows, and urban architecture to frame his characters' isolation. This visual language influenced later works like After Life (1998) and Poetry (2010), which similarly use careful composition to reveal inner emotional states. Yang's approach to depicting technology and business culture in modern Asia also paved the way for films like All About Lily Chou-Chou (2001) and Air Doll (2009). sections.content: Yi Yi's legacy is particularly evident in the way it inspired filmmakers to tackle family dynamics with both scope and intimacy. A Separation (2011) shares its ability to weave personal and societal tensions into a compelling narrative, while The World (2004) similarly explores globalization's impact on personal relationships. Yang's influence can be seen in how Burning (2018) and An Elephant Sitting Still (2018) use extended runtime and careful pacing to build complex character studies.
